registry_info.name: computational_biology
registry_info.description: Computational biology artifacts — limb growth, morphogenesis, protein folding, and radiolarian skeletons. Algorithms that model how living systems build themselves.
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Morphogenesis (Turing), developmental biology, Monte Carlo methods in biochemistry, radiolarian geometry, procedural growth

growslimbs.name: Growing Limbs
growslimbs.description: Procedural limb growth simulation — branching structures emerge from growth rules, mimicking how organisms develop appendages through iterative cell division and differentiation.

limbgrowth.name: Limb Growth
limbgrowth.description: Detailed limb growth and segmentation model — joints, proportions, and symmetry emerging from simple growth parameters. Biology's recipe for building bodies.

monte_carlo_protein.name: Monte Carlo Protein Folding
monte_carlo_protein.description: Protein chain folding using Monte Carlo methods — random conformational changes accepted or rejected by energy minimization. The computational approach to understanding how amino acid sequences become functional 3D shapes.

morphobody.name: Morpho Body
morphobody.description: Morphogenetic body construction — how body plans emerge from developmental rules. From simple gradients to complex anatomies through Turing-like pattern formation.

radiolaria.name: Radiolaria
radiolaria.description: Procedural radiolarian skeleton generation — the impossibly intricate silica structures of single-celled organisms. Geometry so perfect it inspired Ernst Haeckel's 'Art Forms in Nature'.

ten_tulip_buckets.name: Ten Tulip Buckets
ten_tulip_buckets.description: Array of procedurally generated tulip bouquets — each bucket grows tulips from parametric curves with randomized variations. Botanical algorithms producing natural beauty.

MolecularDesigner.name: Molecular Designer
MolecularDesigner.description: Interactive molecular construction tool — atoms snap to valence rules, bonds obey geometry, and molecular structure emerges from chemical constraints. Formalization as hands-on building.
